correctness.rationale: On the no-11 input shift the only possible triples are 000,001,010,100,101; each effective mask therefore represents eight Wolfram rules. Failure of the tests c≠e, not(b=c=d), and not(a=c and b=d) gives collisions of cyclic words (01,10), (001,010), and (1000,0010), respectively, hence also distinct bi-infinite periodic inputs. The successive exclusions have sizes 16,4,2 in mask space, leaving 4,6,7,12,13,18,19,24,25,27. Mask 4 copies the center. For masks 6 and 7, a center 1 guarantees y_i=1 and y_(i+1)=0 because the next triple is 100 or 101. If the center is 0 with y_i=1, the triple is 001 or (for 7) 000, in either case forcing y_(i+1)=1. This proves the right-looking decoder. Reflection gives the left-looking decoder for 12 and 13; bit complement gives the other five masks. These pointwise arguments hold on every allowed input and on all periodic extensions, including repeated indices on short rings. For masks 6 and 7, 010 and 001 give the same new center for different old centers; the reflected and complemented cases inherit the obstruction. Thus only masks 4 and 27 admit radius zero, giving 16 rules. An independent exact loop over all 256 rules, retaining length-n bit strings with no adjacent ones including wraparound and looking for equal encoded outputs, found 128 first collisions at n=2, 32 at n=3, 16 at n=4, and 80 rules without a collision at n≤4. The n=4 failures are masks 5 and 26, including Rule 5; it passes n=1,2,3 and 1000 versus 0010 collides at n=4.
